sections.overview: The high-hat is a western Atlantic drum in the croaker family Sciaenidae, notable for its striped body and elongated dorsal fin.
sections.identification: Adults are pale with several broad dark horizontal bands separated by narrow lines. Juveniles have a distinctive dark mark across the snout and between the eyes.
sections.habitat: After a 2022 taxonomic revision, P. acuminatus is recognized from the U.S. Atlantic coast and Gulf of Mexico; it overlaps P. lineatus in the West Indies and southern Caribbean. Adults use reefs and nearby soft bottoms, to about 113 m.
sections.diet: At night it feeds on crustaceans, polychaete worms, small fishes and zooplankton over sand, mud and rubble close to reefs.
sections.behavior: It shelters by day beneath ledges, among rocks or in reef crevices, then forages after dark; juveniles sometimes shelter in small groups.
sections.reproduction: It is egg-laying; the sources consulted provide little further detail on spawning.
sections.ecology: By moving between reef shelters and nearby soft bottoms to feed, the fish links rocky and sandy benthic habitats. Its close relative P. lineatus occupies the southern part of the complex’s range.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern, assessed in 2023.
